messages:
support_jen: FYI - AcmeCorp reports intermittent failures from JSON mode since ~2026-03-15 22:00 UTC. They see invalid JSON returned ~1-2% of requests. Also noticed a few large latency spikes at the same time. Root cause unclear, escalating to eng/observability. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d.

support_jen: sample response they pasted (from prod):
```
{"order": 12345, "items": [ {"id": "sku-1", "qty": 2}, {"id": "sku-2", "qty": null }], 
"shipping": {"address": "123 Main St"}  // <-- missing closing brace on the outer object in a tiny percentage
```

mike_eng: thanks, can you attach the full request headers and the exact model/version they hit? also want the trace id if available. any common pattern (same prompt, same customer input)?

support_jen: sending the request payload + headers now. Model shown in their dashboard: "redwood-open-3b-v1" (pinned). Trace id on one example: trace=trc-20260315-7f8a. They said it happens on a few different prompts but mostly when customers include nested JSON in user message.

natalie_sre: quick questions: are we confident redaction isn't stripping quotes/braces before logging? support logs are redacted; if we sample payloads for debugging we need to keep PII rules. recommend temporary increased sampling for the failing tenant with on-the-fly redaction rules (hash emails but keep structural punctuation).

mike_eng: agree. also looks like our existing jsonmode parse errors only increment a single counter. We should add a dimensioned metric: jsonmode.parse_error_count{customer,model,error_type} and histograms for response_size and latency. will instrument trace correlation: attach req_id -> span id so we can jump from metric to full trace.

paul_oncall: add to oncall checklist: if json parse rate > 0.5% over 10m for a tenant, page eng-runtime and mark P2. Create a dashboard panel showing parse error rate by model and by tenant with a top-10 sample list.

support_jen: customer also reported a 401 momentarily when toggling plan, but that's separate. for this thread let's focus on parse. they want repro steps we can share with eng.

mike_eng: repro steps request: 1) use their exact prompt (they sent it privately) 2) set model=redwood-open-3b-v1, max_tokens=512, json_mode=true 3) run 1000 requests at low QPS and 1k at burst QPS to try to surface race conditions 4) capture response bodies + req_id + trace id. I've drafted a repro script locally.

support_jen: pasted the private prompt to the thread (redacted here): "user message with nested JSON and some unescaped newlines". customer saw invalid json ~12 times out of 1800 requests in their run.

sara_ml: this smells like schema drift or model output subtlety — the model might be emitting stray comments or trailing commas under certain contexts. we should run evals on the prompt set and diff against previous model versions. also try auto-validate + repair step: run JSON schema validator on model output and if invalid, run a small deterministic repair pass (like wrap in try/catch and run a cleanup LLM pass in non-JSON mode). fallback policy until we fix root cause.

mike_eng: implementation proposal:
- short term: add a sampling hook to persist 1000 raw pre-redaction responses per tenant per day to a secure bucket (access-limited). these are only for debugging and will be rotated.
- observability: new metrics: jsonmode.parse_error_count, jsonmode.repaired_count, jsonmode.latency_histogram; add labels: model, tenant, error_class (missing_comma, trailing_comment, incomplete_object, other).
- tracing: when parse_error triggers, annotate span with parse.error=true and error_class. also attach a link to S3 sample if available.

natalie_sre: make sure any saved pre-redaction payloads pass compliance review. proposed redaction strategy: token-level sampling that preserves punctuation and braces but masks alphanumeric sequences that look like emails/names/SSNs. I'll loop in security for sign-off.

paul_oncall: any chance this is caused by our output streaming path truncating last bytes on socket close? check the streaming code path and the HTTP chunk flush. if streaming client disconnects early we could produce truncated JSON. add a test to simulate client disconnect mid-stream.

mike_eng: good catch. will add a unit/integration test for streaming flush and verify we don't leave incomplete objects in the out buffer. also add a post-filter that validates final output before returning 200; if invalid -> return structured 5xx with error id and increment parse metric so we have visibility.

support_jen: customer wants an ETA and mitigation. they requested turning on an automatic repair fallback for their tenant only until root cause fixed. can we do that?

mike_eng: we can enable tenant-scoped fallback policy (non-JSON fallback to "validated-repair" pipeline) as a config flag. I can roll a toggle to prod as a scoped feature flag (P2) and have it available tomorrow morning PST.

sara_ml: note: fallback has potential to change exact outputs — call it out to customer as best-effort repair. we should also add an integration test that checks that repaired output conforms to schema.

support_jen: will communicate ETA and caveats to AcmeCorp. I'll request permission for increased sampling and send their ok once I have it.

mike_eng: action items I'm taking: create metric PR + dashboard tiles (will link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/420), add streaming-truncation test, and the tenant-scoped fallback toggle. assigning to eng-runtime, ETA: 24h for rollout to canary. tagging @natalie_sre for compliance review for sampling.

natalie_sre: I'll start the compliance review and get back today. also setting an alert rule draft in Grafana and will share the dashboard link once created.

alert-bot: [automated] incident annotation added: tag=structured-output-parse; severity=P2; ticket=INC-2026-317.

support_jen: thanks everyone — I'll update the customer and post back when they approve sampling. If it's helpful, I'll paste a couple more raw failing snippets to help triage.
